headings: Robert Ross Laboratory at UC San Diego
sources.text: Robert Ross Laboratory at UC San Diego Our Research The Ross Lab focuses on understanding the fundamental basis of cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure. Our investigations center on the role of proteins that bridge the extracellular environment to the interior of cells, with particular emphasis on cell-cell and cell-matrix proteins critical for function of cardiac myocytes. More about our research Postdoctoral positions are available. Please E-mail Robert Ross at rross@health.ucsd.edu to inquire. Dr. Robert Ross Principal Investigator Professor of Medicine Assistant Vice-Chancellor for Health Sciences Academic Affairs, Staff Physician, San Diego VA Hospital Co-Director of the Molecular Cardiology Program and Co-director of the Cardiac Biological Science and Engineering Center in the Institute of Engineering in Medicine (IEM). He is also a staff cardiologist and Director of Echocardiography at the San Diego VA Healthcare System. Additional information

sources.title: People - Ross Lab
sources.text: People Robert S. Ross, MD, MBA Principal Investigator Robert S. Ross, MD, MBA is Professor of Medicine, Assistant Vice-Chancellor for Health Sciences Academic Affairs, Co-Director of the Molecular Cardiology Program and Co-director of the Cardiac Biological Science and Engineering Center in the Institute of Engineering in Medicine (IEM). He is also a staff cardiologist and Director of Echocardiography at the San Diego VA Healthcare System. Ross is a physician-scientist with expertise in molecular cardiology, having trained at USC/Keck School of Medicine; Internship and residency at LA County Hospital and Cedars-Sinai Medical center; fellowships at NIH / NHLBI, and UCSD Cardiology program. He has maintained extramural NIH and other national funding for >20 years, with a program focused on the role of cell-matrix and cell-cell adhesion proteins in cardiac physiology, mechanotransduction and disease. Recent work has evolved to also study cell-cell adhesion proteins in cardiac conduction and mitochondrial function in the heart, and extend some of this work to skeletal muscle. He dedicates major efforts towards his research, along with mentoring, training, teaching, and administration. He is an active cardiologist and directs the echocardiography lab at the San Diego VA. Dr. Ross is extensively involved in training postdoctoral research and clinical cardiology fellows, residents and medical students. He is PI of an NIH T32 grant focused on cardiovascular research and also actively mentors faculty. He gained significant experience in entrepreneurship and scientific innovation when he served as site-PI of an NIH funded, Center for Accelerated Innovation award. Dr. Ross is a strong advocate for building the pipeline of diversity in science and medicine. For over 15 years he served as the PI on an NHLBI R25 to support training of underrepresented minority undergraduate students interested in physician-scientist careers, only recently stepping down from this program. He is currently a multi-PI for an NHLBI-funded Program to Increase Diversity among Individuals Engaged in Health-Related Research (PRIDE) at UCSD, mentoring junior faculty from underrepresented backgrounds to achieve academic success.
